description: A doctoral research seminar on designing rules for markets and on how prices form in them: incentive-compatible mechanisms, auctions, equilibria and automated market makers in decentralised exchanges, order books, consensus-level fairness and credit networks. Students read and critique recent papers, formalise and simulate models, and prepare a research proposal with an executable artefact.
modelledOn: Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos and Vazirani (eds.), Algorithmic Game Theory
Hasbrouck, Empirical Market Microstructure and Bouchaud et al., Trades, Quotes and Prices
Cartea, Jaimungal and Penalva, Algorithmic and High-Frequency Trading
Recent conference papers on automated market makers, transaction fee design and order fairness
outcomes: Prove incentive compatibility, individual rationality and revenue properties of auction and mechanism designs.
Model decentralised exchange trading as a game and derive equilibrium and optimal routing results.
Analyse and compare automated market maker designs by their trading functions, liquidity provider returns and loss versus rebalancing.
Apply order book and price-formation models to explain spreads, impact and optimal execution.
Critique front-running, fairness and mechanism proposals for consensus protocols against formal definitions and impossibility results.
Write a research proposal with a precise model, a simulation artefact, a baseline and a stated contribution.

units.title: Foundations of mechanism design
topics: Social choice, Arrow's theorem and the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem
Bayesian games, dominant-strategy and Bayes-Nash incentive compatibility
The revelation principle and quasi-linear utilities
The VCG mechanism, its limits and the impossibility of efficient bilateral trade
Computational mechanism design: tractability versus incentive compatibility

units.title: Auctions
topics: First-price, second-price, English and Dutch auctions; revenue equivalence
Optimal auctions: virtual values and reserve prices
Combinatorial auctions and spectrum allocation
Position auctions and sponsored search with generalised second price
Simple versus optimal mechanisms and prior-independent design
Transaction fee mechanism design: first-price versus posted-price fees and incentive compatibility for block producers

units.title: Equilibrium in decentralised exchanges
topics: Constant function market makers as games between traders, arbitrageurs and liquidity providers
Nash and Stackelberg equilibria in trade routing; price of anarchy
No-arbitrage pricing and convex analysis of trading functions
Optimal routing and batch trades as convex programmes; existence and uniqueness of equilibria
Empirical stylised facts of decentralised exchange volume, fees and liquidity

units.title: Automated market maker design and optimisation
topics: Constant-sum, constant-product and constant-mean invariants; trading function design
Concentrated liquidity, tick design and range orders
Impermanent loss and loss versus rebalancing; the replication argument
Dynamic fees and oracle-informed market makers
Cost-function market makers and the logarithmic market scoring rule for prediction markets
Liquidity provision as portfolio optimisation under fee income and adverse selection

units.title: Order book models and price formation
topics: Limit order book mechanics: matching, price-time priority and order types
Adverse selection models of the spread: sequential-trade and informed-trader models
Market impact: the square-root law and optimal execution
Queueing and point-process models of the order book, including Hawkes processes
Market making with inventory risk: the optimal quoting model
Call auctions, frequent batch auctions and continuous trading compared

units.title: Front-running and fairness in consensus
topics: Extractable value: front-running, back-running and sandwich attacks; a taxonomy
Order fairness definitions, Condorcet cycles and impossibility results
Mitigations: commit-reveal, threshold encryption and batch auctions
Proposer-builder separation, block-building auctions and centralisation
Latency, geography and fairness for participants in Africa

units.title: Credit networks and liquidity
topics: Credit networks and trust lines: payment routing as max-flow
Payment channel networks: liquidity, rebalancing and routing fees
Clearing, netting and contagion in financial networks
Mobile-money float, interoperability and community currencies as credit networks

units.title: Open research problems and project
topics: Survey of open problems across mechanism design and market microstructure
Formalising a research question: model, assumptions and metrics
Simulation and empirical methodology; artefact evaluation
Proposal writing and peer review

schedule.title: Social choice and incentive compatibility
schedule.exercise: Read and summarise the proof sketch of the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem, and show with the revelation principle why truthful mechanisms lose no generality.

tasks.title: Compute outcomes of plurality, Borda and pairwise-majority rules on 8 preference profiles and find a profile where one voter gains by misreporting
Check Bayes-Nash incentive compatibility of a given two-bidder mechanism by best-response search on a discretised value grid
Convert an indirect mechanism with a known equilibrium into a direct truthful mechanism via the revelation principle and verify it numerically

schedule.title: VCG and its limits
schedule.exercise: Prove the VCG mechanism is dominant-strategy truthful, and critique the impossibility result for bilateral trade.

tasks.title: Compute VCG payments for 4 bidders and 3 items with given values, then check truthful reporting is optimal for each bidder
Simulate bilateral trade with uniform values, compute the efficiency loss of the best budget-balanced mechanism, and compare it with first-best
Compare an exact VCG allocation with a greedy approximation on knapsack-style combinatorial instances and measure the loss in truthfulness incentives

schedule.title: Classical auctions and optimal design
schedule.exercise: Derive revenue equivalence for first- and second-price auctions, and compute the optimal reserve price for uniform and exponential values.

tasks.title: Simulate first-price and second-price auctions with equilibrium bidding for 10,000 draws and verify that average revenue matches
Compute virtual values and the optimal reserve price for a value distribution and plot revenue against the reserve price
Implement a simple combinatorial auction winner determination solver and test it on 10 generated instances against a greedy approximation

schedule.title: Position auctions, simplicity and fee mechanisms
schedule.exercise: Compare generalised second price with VCG for sponsored search, and critique a transaction fee mechanism paper against incentive properties.

tasks.title: Compute equilibrium bids and revenue for generalised second price and VCG in a 3-slot auction and plot revenue against click-through rates
Compare a posted-price mechanism with the optimal auction on regular value distributions and measure the revenue ratio over 100 random instances
Simulate a first-price fee auction and a posted-price fee mechanism with a strategic block producer, and measure fee volatility and producer gain

schedule.title: Games on decentralised exchanges
schedule.exercise: Model a swap as a strategic interaction between a trader and an arbitrageur, and prove existence and uniqueness of the no-arbitrage pool state.

tasks.title: Plot the constant-product curve, compute the output and slippage of swaps of increasing size, and find the arbitrage trade that restores an outside price
Solve the optimal split of one large trade across three pools as a convex programme and compare the output with routing through a single pool
Simulate best-response dynamics between traders routing through shared pools and measure the price of anarchy against the optimal routing

schedule.title: Trading functions and concentrated liquidity
schedule.exercise: Compare the constant-sum, constant-product and constant-mean invariants, and derive impermanent loss for a price move of a given size.

tasks.title: Plot reserves and marginal prices for three trading functions, identify which has bounded slippage, and read the price impact of a swap
Simulate a concentrated liquidity position in a price range over a random price path and compute fees earned against holding
Simulate loss versus rebalancing against a continuous price process, and compare the result with the closed-form expression

schedule.title: Dynamic fees, prediction markets and liquidity provision
schedule.exercise: Design a dynamic fee that depends on volatility, and show the bounded loss of the logarithmic market scoring rule.

tasks.title: Compute prices and payments for a logarithmic market scoring rule on a three-outcome market and verify the worst-case loss bound
Simulate a pool with a volatility-based fee against a fixed fee under informed and uninformed flow and compare liquidity provider profit
Choose a liquidity range and capital for a provider under fee income and adverse selection, optimise expected utility, and test it out of sample

schedule.title: Order books and adverse selection
schedule.exercise: Derive the spread in a sequential-trade setting, and solve the optimal execution trajectory for a large order with temporary and permanent impact.

tasks.title: Step a limit order book through 20 events with price-time priority and record the book, the trades and the spread after each event
Simulate a sequential-trade market maker facing informed traders and plot the quoted spread against the share of informed trading
Compute the optimal execution schedule for a large order with impact and risk aversion, and plot cost against the trading horizon

schedule.title: Order flow models, market making and batch auctions
schedule.exercise: Fit a simple point-process model to order arrivals, derive optimal quotes under inventory risk, and compare batch with continuous trading.

tasks.title: Simulate a self-exciting Hawkes order arrival process and compare the clustering of events with a Poisson process by plotting inter-arrival times
Simulate an inventory-aware market maker for 1,000 time steps and compare profit and inventory variance with symmetric quoting
Compare frequent batch auctions with continuous trading under a latency-advantaged trader and measure the transfer from slower participants

schedule.title: Extractable value and order fairness
schedule.exercise: Classify extractable value strategies, state a formal order-fairness definition, and show why Condorcet cycles prevent a perfect fair ordering.

tasks.title: Simulate a sandwich attack on a constant-product pool, compute the attacker's profit and the victim's extra slippage, and find the slippage setting that prevents it
Build the pairwise precedence graph for 6 transactions seen by 5 nodes, find any Condorcet cycle, and propose an ordering
Simulate commit-reveal and batch-auction ordering against a front-running adversary and measure the adversary's gain under each rule

schedule.title: Block building and geography
schedule.exercise: Model proposer-builder separation as an auction, assess centralisation risks, and analyse how network latency from Africa affects fairness.

tasks.title: Simulate a block-building auction among builders of different sizes and measure how often the largest builder wins as its order flow advantage grows
Place nodes in Accra, Lagos and Frankfurt on a network model with realistic latencies and measure who sees a transaction first
Fit a model of builder market share against order flow advantage and use it to project the concentration under three policy options

schedule.title: Credit networks, channels and contagion
schedule.exercise: Model a payment network as a capacity graph, find the maximum payment, and trace default contagion through a network of banks.

tasks.title: Compute the maximum flow between two parties in a credit network and show the residual capacity after the payment
Simulate a payment channel network with random payments, track channel imbalance, and compare routing policies by success rate
Compute clearing payments for a network of 8 institutions after a shock and find the node whose failure causes the largest cascade

schedule.title: Open problems and research proposal
schedule.exercise: Write and present a research proposal with a precise question, model, baseline, simulation plan and expected contribution.

tasks.title: Write the model of your proposed question as equations with stated assumptions, and check them on a small closed-form special case
Build a simulation artefact for your model with fixed seeds, run it against one baseline, and produce one figure with confidence bands
Review three anonymised proposals in a case, score each against a rubric for novelty and soundness, and write the report you would give the author
